newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 80 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 80 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 50 billion bolivar ($103 million) auction of 178-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 23.00 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 15 billion bolivars ($30 million) in 269-day bills with a 23.66 percent coupon, and another 15 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 24.33 percent coupon.
Some 80 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are up from last week's 61.98 billion bolivar issue. Then 177-, 266- and 358-day notes carried 20.15, 20.65, and 21.18 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that rose some three percentage points along the curve to 22.99, 24.89 and 25.66 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
